newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU consumers should choose on gene foods -Fischler.
newsitem.headline: EU consumers should choose on gene foods -Fischler.

text.p: European consumers should be given the choice of whether or not to buy genetically modified foodstuffs, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday.

"We do have a large measure of agreement that it should be up to the consumer to decide whether he buys GMO products or not," Fischler told the European Parliament's agriculture and rural development committee.
But Fischler added that in the long term Europe would need to use gene technology.
"We can't do without it in the pharmceutical industry today and we won't be able to do without it in agriculture tomorrow," he said.
The EU must decide how to use gene technology, which products to authorise or ban and the labelling of such items, he added.
European Commission President Jacques Santer is due shortly to present compromise proposals on the labelling of genetically modified food.
Fischler has been seeking segregation of GMO products throughout the food chain and compulsory labelling.
He has argued that alternative proposals for less stringent labelling rules, stating that food "may contain" GMO products, would be meaningless.
